content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Erika Bolton (E002)
Requested access: admin to Payroll

Notes:
- HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say full-time Analyst, recommendation write.
- Security says contractor with basic security training, recommendation read.

The conflict here is between full-time and contractor status. Most notes say full-time, but Security says contractor.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does). So max for full-time = write.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. Security says basic training, so max = read.

Either way, the requested admin exceeds maximum. The maximum is either write (full-time) or read (contractor).

Which is correct? The majority consensus says full-time Analyst. The Security note says contractor. Hmm. We need to decide the final level.

Given the conflicting information, what's the right decision? The policy says never grant more than requested. Requested is admin. If we go with full-time (majority), the max is write, so grant write. If we go with contractor, the max is read, grant read.

The evidence is conflicting. Typically, we might consider which facts are reliable. There are 5 notes saying full-time, 1 saying contractor. Majority favors full-time. But security might have authoritative info? The instructions don't say one agent is more authoritative.

I should probably go with the majority / most consistent information: full-time Analyst, so max write. Grant write since requested admin exceeds max.

Let me submit write with reasoning citing the policy and majority of notes.

Actually, let me reconsider. The decision should be based on available information. Given conflicting employee facts, I need to make a judgment. Most of the team (5 of 6) say full-time. One says contractor. I'll follow the majority and grant write.

I'll submit decision: write.
